title: How To Perform Bulgarian Split Squats | Legs Exercise Tutorial
creator: Buff Dudes Workouts
description:
How To Perform Bulgarian Split Squats

👉GRAB our 🔴HOME GYM WORKOUT PLAN🔴 here: https://bit.ly/homegymplan

🍖🥦 Buff Dudes Cookbook: https://www.buffdudes.us/products/b-u...

😎 JOIN THE BUFF CLUB: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKf0UqBiCQI4Ol0To9V0pKQ/join

The Bulgarian split squat is an excellent unilateral movement that helps with strength, stabilization and imbalances. It primarily works the quadriceps and gluteal muscles, but will also include the hamstrings, and core. 

How to: 

Place an elevated platform onto the ground at a height that is comfortable - or use a bench if needed. 
Elevate one foot onto the platform or bench and step your other foot away from the bench. 
The distance of your foot that is placed onto the ground will differ from person to person, so play with the placement until you reach a comfortable position. 
Keep a vertical torso as you flex in the hip and knee, squatting down until your thigh is parallel with the ground. 
Extend in your hip and knee joint to squat upward until you reach the starting position. 
Feel free to add weight to this exercise by holding a pair of dumbbells. 

Do not:

DO NOT place your foot too close as this will decrease your range of motion and force your heel to elevate off of the floor. 
DO NOT lean forward. Leaning forward will throw your balance off and force your spine out of a neutral position. 
DO NOT place your foot too far forward. By placing your foot too far forward you’ll decrease your range of motion and increase the stretch in the hamstrings. 

The bulgarian squat is essentially a slightly assisted single leg squat, focusing on pinpointing one leg at a time. Use this as a way to target imbalances and deficiencies in either of your legs, or a way to place more stimulation in your quads and glutes.

title: Dumbbell Romanian (RDL) Deadlift |TECHNIQUE for Beginners
creator: Mike | J2FIT Strength & Conditioning
description:
How to do the dumbbell Romanian deadlift (RDL) for hamstrings and glutes — proper form for beginners.

FREE dumbbell training plan → https://j2fit.com/programs/dumbbell

The dumbbell RDL is the single best hamstring and glute builder you can do without a barbell. It's a hip hinge, not a squat — and that distinction is why most people feel it in their low back instead of their hamstrings.

0:00 Introduction to RDL
0:21 Performing the movement
0:50 Common mistakes to avoid

HOW TO DO IT:
- Set a soft bend in your knees and FREEZE it there
- Push your hips straight back, chest stays proud
- Lower until you feel a deep hamstring stretch — usually mid-shin
- Drive your hips forward to stand, squeeze glutes at the top

COMMON MISTAKES:
- Bending down instead of hinging back
- Letting the knees travel forward (turns it into a squat)
- Rounding the lower back at the bottom
- Going too heavy before you own the hinge

SETS & REPS: 3-4 sets of 8-12 reps

title: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat (Full Tutorial) - Single Leg Exercise for QUADS
creator: Mike | J2FIT Strength & Conditioning
description:
Dumbbell Bulgarian split squat — single leg exercise for quads and glutes, full form breakdown.

FREE dumbbell training plan → https://j2fit.com/programs/dumbbell

The Bulgarian split squat builds more leg mass per pound of load than almost anything else, because one leg is doing all the work. Foot position decides whether it hits quads or glutes.

FOR QUADS: stand closer to the bench, stay upright, let the knee travel forward
FOR GLUTES: step further out, hinge the torso forward slightly

HOW TO DO IT:
- Rear foot on a bench, front foot far enough out to stay balanced
- Lower straight down, front shin controls the depth
- Drive through the front heel and midfoot
- Keep the rear leg passive — it's a kickstand, not a working leg

COMMON MISTAKES:
- Stance too short (knee jams forward, balance goes)
- Pushing off the back foot
- Torso collapsing forward when the weight gets heavy

SETS & REPS: 3 sets of 8-12 per leg
